daily_brief: The day's most consequential development is Hamas's agreement to disarm under a US-brokered framework, marking what could be the most significant step toward ending the nearly three-year Gaza war [BBC, France 24, Le Monde]. The deal, announced by President Trump's Board of Peace, provides for weapons storage under Palestinian oversight rather than direct handover to Israel, with Israeli withdrawal to proceed as disarmament is completed. In Europe, a massive humanitarian crisis unfolded as approximately 49,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's Ceuta enclave within 24 hours, leaving at least 18 dead and prompting military deployment [BBC, France 24, The Guardian, Globe and Mail]. The crossing followed a Spanish Supreme Court ruling barring summary returns of migrants stopped at sea. UEFA's unanimous vote to boycott FIFA World Cups if private investor plans proceed has created an unprecedented rift in global football governance [BBC, France 24, Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, Hungary faces potential energy crisis as record-low Danube water levels force shutdown of its sole nuclear plant [BBC], and a Russian missile that struck Polish territory has escalated NATO tensions [BBC].

top_stories.headline: Hamas Agrees to Disarmament Framework in Potential Breakthrough for Gaza Peace
bullets: Hamas confirmed agreement to a Board of Peace plan for complete disarmament in Gaza, with weapons to be inventoried and stored under Palestinian supervision rather than handed to Israel
US President Trump announced Israeli forces would withdraw from Gaza as disarmament is completed, calling it a critical step toward a new Palestinian government
The deal follows months of negotiations and comes shortly after Hamas elected Gaza-based leader Khalil al-Hayya as head of the movement
Israel has not yet commented on the agreement; implementation remains uncertain

top_stories.headline: Nearly 50,000 Migrants Enter Spanish Ceuta in 24 Hours, At Least 18 Dead
bullets: Spanish officials estimate approximately 49,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta by land and sea within 24 hours, more than half the city's population
At least 18 people died in the crossing, including drownings and deaths in a crush at the Tarajal beach breakwater fence
Spain deployed military forces to reinforce Civil Guard; Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited Ceuta on Friday
The mass crossing followed a Spanish Supreme Court ruling this month barring summary returns of migrants stopped at sea near Ceuta or Melilla

top_stories.headline: UEFA Votes Unanimously to Boycott FIFA World Cups Over Private Investor Plan
bullets: All 55 UEFA member associations voted to withdraw from World Cups and other FIFA competitions if private investor plan proceeds
CONCACAF's 41 member associations also rejected FIFA President Gianni Infantino's proposal to sell up to 20% stake in commercial subsidiary
FIFA responded defiantly, pledging to continue consultations and stating 'nobody is selling football'
The proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise could be valued at $20 billion, with Thrive Capital expected to lead investor group

top_stories.headline: Hungary to Shut Down Only Nuclear Plant as Danube Hits Record Lows
bullets: Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant will shut down entirely for the first time due to Danube water levels too low for cooling system suction nozzles
Prime Minister Péter Magyar warned energy supply could become critical from Monday during ongoing heatwave with temperatures around 37°C
Government asked citizens to limit energy-intensive activities during peak hours; rotational shutdowns possible if conservation insufficient
Romania has also shut down one of two reactors at Cernavoda plant due to low water levels; Danube at 30-year lows across multiple countries

top_stories.headline: Russian Cruise Missile Strikes Polish Territory During Major Ukraine Attack
bullets: A missile, identified as likely a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, crashed into a field in eastern Poland 92km from the Ukrainian border, leaving a 10-meter crater
Polish PM Donald Tusk confirmed the armed missile violated NATO airspace during a large-scale Russian attack that killed at least eight people near Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine
Five members of the Voronov family, including three children, were killed when a missile destroyed their home; five other family members remain missing
NATO said it was in close contact with Polish authorities; Poland stated it was prepared to shoot down the missile if it had continued its flight

sources.name: BBC Europe
